more_info.overview: Gelatine is a mixture of animal-derived proteins obtained by partially breaking down collagen. It absorbs water and softens in cold water, then dissolves when heated. On cooling, the solution forms a gel, which explains its gelling function in food. JECFA also identifies stabilising, emulsifying and crystallisation-control functions. The commercial ingredient can be supplied as sheets, flakes or powder, with grades that differ in gel strength.
more_info.origin: Gelatine is manufactured by partially hydrolysing collagen from animal tissues such as skin, tendons, ligaments and bones. The protein is extracted and processed into dried sheets, flakes or powder. It is an animal-derived ingredient; the specification does not identify a single animal species for every product.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: Ordinary gelatine is made from animal collagen and is therefore unsuitable for vegan and vegetarian diets. Halal and kosher suitability depend on the animal species, slaughter and processing arrangements, and product certification; the E code alone does not establish those conditions.
